script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so the CIN @ PIT script is form-only. CIN QB Joe Burrow is +0.27 EPA/dropback when not blitzed, while PIT QB Aaron Rodgers is negative either way (-0.36 vs blitz, n=23; -0.42 with no blitz), so the base case is a competitive game with CIN the more functional offense: CIN RB Chase Brown keeps the rush share (36 carries, 136 yards) and CIN WR Tee Higgins stays the downfield target (16 targets, 210 air yards). PIT blitzes 25%, enough for some quick throws, not enough to assume the game flips. Who leads by halftime is unknown without a market line.
script.flip1: PIT makes the blitz the plan and CIN QB Burrow's -0.62 EPA on 24 blitzed dropbacks shows up. CIN falls behind, CIN RB Brown's carries die, and CIN WR Higgins' deep air yards stall in favor of CIN checkdowns (Brown 11 targets at -27 air yards, CIN TE Mike Gesicki, CIN RB Samaje Perine).
script.flip2: CIN gets ahead and drains the clock. CIN RB Brown's carries spike into a PIT run defense that has allowed 4.54 YPC and seven 10-plus runs, while the PIT Warren/Dowdle committee has to throw and CIN WR volume cools late.

matchup.shell: No CIN or PIT coverage charting, so MOFO/MOFC and man/zone are unknown. Location splits are the proxy: PIT allowed 9.1 YPA left (20 att) and 8.53 right (17 att) but 3.43 middle (7 att) — PIT outside leaks, PIT middle looks closed on a tiny sample. CIN allowed 8.89 middle (18 att) and 8.04 left (28 att) but 5.11 right (36 att).
matchup.pressure: PIT blitz rate 25%. CIN QB Burrow is -0.62 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=24) and +0.27 with no blitz — that split is the CIN kill switch, but blitz rate is not pressure rate (not in pack). CIN blitzes only 11%, and PIT QB Rodgers is poor either way, so CIN does not need pressure to bother PIT.
matchup.bleeds: PIT run defense bleeds: 4.54 YPC and 7 runs of 10+ in two games, plus 7 passes of 20+ on only 51 attempts. CIN is tighter on explosive runs (4.05 YPC, 4 runs of 10+) and on explosive passes by rate (7 of 90) but CIN bleeds the middle (8.89 YPA) and the left (8.04); CIN's right side is the firm zone (5.11 on 36 att).
matchup.overlap: Core overlap is CIN RB Chase Brown's carry share into PIT's 4.54 YPC and seven 10-plus runs. Second overlap is CIN WR Tee Higgins' downfield role (210 air yards, team-high CIN targets) into PIT's leaky left/right YPA and 20+ rate. The counter-overlap is PIT's 25% blitz into CIN QB Burrow's -0.62 blitz EPA, which would move the ball to CIN checkdowns and off Higgins. PIT TE Pat Freiermuth into CIN's soft middle is real, but 37.5 sits on his ~39-yard two-game pace, so it is not a priced edge.

form: CIN and PIT packs are two-game aggregates (weeks [1, 2], labeled L3) with no single-game splits, so one explosive week could be hidden. CIN RB Chase Brown 36/136 is about 18 carries and 68 rush yards per game at 3.78 YPC, plus 11 targets for only 24 yards — CIN rush volume is real, receiving yards are not. CIN WR Tee Higgins 16/154/210 is about 77 rec yards per game and is the CIN passing engine; CIN WR Ja'Marr Chase 13/87/115 is about 43.5 per game, and fading him under 77 loses the counter-case, so no Chase leg. CIN TE Gesicki 7/78/63 (~39 per game, 11.1 yards per target) is low-volume efficiency and treated as fluky. PIT WR DK Metcalf 19 targets and 266 air yards produced only 67 yards — opportunity without production, so a PIT under is a regression trap. PIT RB Jaylen Warren 21/89 (~44.5 rush per game) with PIT RB Rico Dowdle 15/37 is a committee. PIT QB Rodgers 1 carry for 5 yards makes the 0.5 rush line noise.

edge_players.edge_sentence: CIN RB Chase Brown has taken 36 of Cincinnati's listed carries for 136 yards, and PIT has allowed 4.54 yards per carry with seven runs of 10-plus, so 63.5 sits under the CIN workload he has already had.

edge_players.edge_sentence: CIN WR Tee Higgins leads Cincinnati in targets, yards, and air yards (16/154/210, about 77 per game) and PIT has leaked to both outside zones (9.1 left, 8.53 right) with seven 20-plus passes on 51 attempts, so 54.5 is short of the CIN role he has played.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both CIN overs lost because the missing spread hid a PIT lead. PIT blitzed after seeing CIN QB Burrow at -0.62 EPA on 24 blitzed dropbacks, CIN trailed by the second quarter, and CIN RB Brown never saw his 18-carry pace — CIN RB Perine took the checkdowns and 63.5 rush yards was too high. CIN WR Higgins' 154 yards were one week-1 explosive that did not travel; with weather unsaved and PIT's middle the only firm zone (3.43 YPA on 7 attempts), the ball went underneath to CIN TE Gesicki and CIN RB Brown and Higgins finished in the 30s. A two-game CIN/PIT aggregate and no inactives list were not enough to know the target tree.

They win together if CIN stays competitive and CIN QB Burrow is mostly unhurried; they lose together if the PIT blitz flip puts CIN in a hole.
